previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, COPD, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for worsening right leg cellulitis. Evaluation ruled out DVT but revealed signs concerning for osteomyelitis, leading to a PICC line placement for long-term IV antibiotics. She was also treated for a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli and managed for delirium, anemia, and a chronic leg ulcer. Her condition stabilized over nine days, with improvement in infection and mental status. She was discharged on home IV antibiotics with nursing support, follow-up arranged with multiple specialists, and education on wound care, diabetes management, and CPAP compliance.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with history of COPD and HFpEF 
who presented with dyspnea, found to have hypercapneic 
respiratory failure. 

BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
# Hypercapneic respiratory failure: The patient presented with 
worsening dyspnea over the past 2 days in the setting of 
nebulizer non-compliance. Labs on presentation remarkable for 
pCO2 110, BNP elevated to 4529. Hypercapneic respiratory failure 
was thought to be multifactorial due to both COPD, baseline 
restrictive lung disease and HFpEF exacerbation (see below). The 
patient was intubated on presentation. Her home nebulizers were 
transitioned to MDI while intubated. She was diuresed with 
intermittent IV Lasix and Lasix gtt with improvement in her 
respiratory status. She was extubated on ___. The patient 
was restarted on her home albuterol nebs and duonebs. The 
patient was transferred to the floor on ___. While on the 
floor, patient refused to wear CPAP overnight and had an episode 
of apnea and unresponsiveness - thought to be due to CPAP 
noncompliance in the setting of COPD. The patient was monitored 
in the ICU subsequently until ___ and her respiratory status 
stabilized.  

# Acute on Chronic Diastolic Heart Failure: Most recent TTE 
___ showed preserved EF (50-55%), mild symmetric LVH. The 
patient presented with elevated BNP and CXR with moderate 
pulmonary edema concerning for diastolic heart failure 
exacerbation. Unclear trigger of exacerbation, possibly 
medication non-adherence or dietary indiscretion. The patient 
was diuresed with Lasix gtt as well as intermittent IV bolus of 
120mg. The patient was evaluated with repeat TTE which showed 
worsening MR and TR as well as possibly worsened RV systolic 
function (though it was thought that prior RV function may have 
been overestimated).   After the lasix drip, she was treated 
with torsemide, 80 mg, and then 80 mg po bid, with goal of 
keeping her even.  She did have creatinine elevation with 
diuresis. Dry weight is not yet established.  

# COPD Exacerbation: Reported history of worsening dyspnea for 2 
days without using nebulizers raises concern for COPD 
exacerbation. The patient was restarted on her home nebulizers. 
Held off on steroid treatment. 

# Bradycardia with junctional rhythm on dopamine gtt: Patient 
developed sinus bradycardia shortly after sedation and 
intubation, initially felt to be consistent with a vagal 
reaction. However, patient subsequently was noted to have 
frequent atrial ectopy followed by sinus arrest vs. sinus exit 
block, with a prolonged junctional rhythm and eventual recovery 
of sinus node with persistent sinus bradycardia. Concern for 
sick sinus syndrome, given patient's history of AFib. The 
patient's BP was supported with dopamine gtt. Her HR stabilized 
and she was weaned of dopamine gtt with stabilization in BP. 

# Acute Kidney Injury: Likely iatrogenic due to aggressive 
diuresis. Peak Cr (1.5), from baseline (0.9). Resolving to 1.1 
on discharge.

#Sepsis with presumed pyelonephritis: During hospitalization, 
the patient developed AMS and increased RR, meeting new sepsis 
guidelines. Pt was found to have RUQ pain and CVA tenderness, as 
well as R > L erythema and tenderness. Given her multiple 
antibiotic allergies, she was started on daptomycin and 
meropenam to provide broad spectrum coverage, including VRE 
(grew out VRE >100,000 colonies in urine culture during 
admission although without symptoms and bland urinalysis). 
Mental status and leukocytosis resolved with antibiotics. No 
growth on urine or blood culture. She was switched to PO 
linezolid to provide VRE coverage for presumed pyelonephritis. 
At discharge, she was afebrile, alert and oriented, with no 
localizing symptoms on exam. Fluoxetine with discontinued on 
admission due to concern for medication interaction.

# Goals of Care: The patient was evaluated by palliative care 
while hospitalized to clarify goals of care as the patient had 
many recent admissions for respiratory failure, but left the 
hospital AMA before these issues could be addressed in prior 
hosptializations. Patient confirmed her wishes for aggressive 
care, even in situations where she is refusing. Please see 
palliative care note for further details.

# Depression: Patient was restarted home lamotrigine it was 
unclear why the patient was taking this medication.  Fluoxetine 
and trazodone held on discharge due to interaction with 
linezolid.

# Coronary Artery Disease: Patient was continued on home aspirin 
and simvastatin. Metoprolol initially held due to bradycardia, 
but restarted. Candesartan held due to ___ as above. Please 
restart with creatinine stable.

CHRONIC ISSUES
# Type 2 DM: The patient's home metformin was held during 
admission. She was uptitrated on lantus while hospitalized.

# Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Patient was continued on home 
rivaroxaban 

# HTN: held home metoprolol in the setting of hypotension and 
bradycardia.

# Alcohol Dependency, Polysubstance Abuse: continued thiamine

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the intensive care unit for not being able 
to breathe. You had a breathing tube in and needed to breathe 
with a mechanical ventilator. You had a lot of fluid in your 
lungs, and needed a a lot of Lasix. On the floor you had a scary 
episode where you didn't breathe and didn't respond, so you were 
sent back to the ICU for further monitoring. We felt that your 
breathing was OK at time of discharge.

You were also kept in the hospital due to an infection, which 
made you briefly confused. We believe the infection is most 
likely in your kidneys, and you were started on antibiotics. 
Your symptoms and laboratory tests improved, so we believe the 
antibiotics are effectively treating your infection. You will 
continue taking antibiotics at home.

As we discussed, at length, we would strongly urge you to 
consider a CPAP or BiPAP machine at home.

Please use your new nebulizer machine.

Please weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up 
more than 3 lbs. Please continue your home dose of Lasix, which 
was been restarted here in the hospital.

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___.

Sincerely, 
Your Team at ___
